summary.headline: 1000000035: estimated recovery below the cost of a demand
summary.rationale: 1000000035 billed 99215 on 36.2% of 1,830 claims against an expected 4.3% given patient complexity (risk-adjusted score 26.92; plain z-score vs peers 5.62). 58% of this provider's 99215 claims were on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Records came back for 30 claims. Of 9 documented 99215 claims, 1 (11%) were documented below the billed level, against 41% for the comparison providers. Note checks on 30 returned notes (share showing each sign): problems 60%, late 13%, unsigned 0%, data 27%. No audit trail was received. 16 of 25 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line on the claim. This pattern is consistent with upcoding. It is a reason to review the records, not a finding. Examples: C0019839: billed 99215; documented MDM level moderate, 30 minutes. C0018873: billed 99215, patient aged 70 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0018931: billed 99215, patient aged 42 with 0 chronic condition(s). C0019126: billed 99215, patient aged 37 with 1 chronic condition(s) (COPD). No demand is sent: the estimated recovery (lower bound $0) is below the staff cost of a demand ($507).
next_steps: Request the full charts for C0019839, C0018873, C0018931 and have a certified coder re-score each against the current E/M rules (medical decision making or total time).
If the re-scoring confirms the pattern, review the random sample in the recovery packet's sampling plan before any overpayment estimate; do not extrapolate from a targeted sample.
Look at the notes themselves: 60% address fewer problems than their level implies and 13% were signed late; request the audit trail for C0019839, C0018873, C0018931.
